sEn: Lauren explains how Grok Bot lets companies build always-on AI teammates with their own identities, tools, and credentials.
sZh: Lauren 讲述 Grok Bot 如何让企业打造拥有独立身份、工具与凭证、始终在线的 AI 同事。

consensus.en: Grok Bot organizes work around AI teammates with identities, tools, and always-on proactivity, not chats or files.
consensus.zh: Grok Bot 以 AI 队友为核心组织工作，赋予其身份、工具与常驻主动性，而非围绕聊天或文件。

consensus.en: Bots should use the same tools humans do, including their own computer, credentials, and Slack presence.
consensus.zh: 机器人应使用与人类相同的工具，包括自己的电脑、凭证和 Slack 身份。

consensus.en: Trust builds in stages: read-only bots first, then action-taking, then owning an entire job.
consensus.zh: 信任分阶段建立：先只读，再能行动，最后承担完整职责。

consensus.en: The smallest useful loop is teaching agents to run code and check their own work empirically.
consensus.zh: 最小有效闭环是教智能体运行代码并实证检验自己的工作。

consensus.en: Encode quality into the codebase via lint rules and static analysis so agents need fewer review tokens.
consensus.zh: 通过 lint 规则和静态分析把质量编码进代码库，让智能体少花审查 token。

consensus.en: As execution becomes abundant, the bottleneck shifts to intent specification, vision, and taste.
consensus.zh: 当执行变得充裕，瓶颈转向意图定义、产品愿景与品味。

contrarian.en: Small businesses, not AI-forward engineers, are among the most enthusiastic early adopters out of hiring necessity.
contrarian.zh: 最热情的早期用户反而是因招人困难而被迫采用的小企业，而非 AI 前沿工程师。

contrarian.en: More adversarial review is not always better; agents overfit to feedback lacking product judgment.
contrarian.zh: 更多对抗式审查未必更好，智能体易过拟合缺乏产品判断的反馈。

contrarian.en: Agents merging their own pull requests works when guardrails are encoded, not because review is skipped.
contrarian.zh: 智能体自行合并 PR 可行，前提是护栏已编码，而非跳过审查。

contrarian.en: Shipping every feature fast is wrong; default is not shipping without internal product-market fit.
contrarian.zh: 快速上线每个功能是错的；未获内部产品市场契合就不上线是默认规则。

contrarian.en: Bots lack social awareness in Slack threads and don't know who the domain expert or decision-maker is.
contrarian.zh: 机器人在 Slack 线程中缺乏社交意识，分不清谁是领域专家或决策者。

contrarian.en: Fast, cheap, and high quality are no longer a pick-two trade-off; all three are now achievable.
contrarian.zh: 快、便宜、高质量不再是三选二，如今三者可以兼得。

turns.en: Grok Bot is meant to be this product where you can create AI teammates. They have their own identity, their own telephone number, credit card, like basically almost anything a human can do. I think we would want bots to do. I sort of see myself as the explorer, trying to figure out what software engineering looks like 6 months to a year from now. Welcome back to another episode of The Light Cone. Today we're joined by Lauren Tan and Roman Ugarte, the team behind Grok Bot. Roman and Lauren incubated the product and are on the core team that took it from the first line of code to launch in just seven weeks. Lauren, Roman, welcome to The Light Cone.
turns.zh: Grok Bot 旨在成为这样一个产品：你可以创建 AI 队友。它们有自己的身份、自己的电话号码、信用卡，几乎人类能做的任何事情，我认为我们都希望机器人能做。我把自己看作探索者，试图弄清楚 6 个月到一年后的软件工程会是什么样子。欢迎回到 The Light Cone 的另一期节目。今天我们的嘉宾是 Lauren Tan 和 Roman Ugarte，他们是 Grok Bot 背后的团队。Roman 和 Lauren 孵化了这个产品，并且是核心团队成员，从第一行代码到发布仅用了七周时间。Lauren、Roman，欢迎来到 The Light Cone。

turns.en: Thanks for having us.
turns.zh: 感谢邀请我们。

turns.en: Thanks so much for having us.
turns.zh: 非常感谢邀请我们。

turns.en: So, we're at this crazy moment where Grok Bot is out there. It's used by a whole lot of people. It is very, very easy to get started. I just noticed Grok Bot is built into the default DM now on X, which is really cool. What is it and how are both people and businesses using it right now?
turns.zh: 所以，我们正处于这样一个疯狂的时刻：Grok Bot 已经面世。它被很多人使用。上手非常非常容易。我刚刚注意到 Grok Bot 现在已经内置到 X 的默认私信中，这真的很酷。它是什么？现在个人和企业是如何使用它的？

turns.en: Many of you have tried it, but for those who haven't, Grok Bot is meant to be this product where you can create AI teammates, and we mean that seriously. You can give these teammates names and identities and functions and skills and tools and all of these things. And I think where Grok Bot came from for us is it was initially this internal prototype that we spun up in a very short amount of time. We spun it up in about seven weeks. And we did it partially because we'd seen the way that AI coding had completely transformed the way that our engineers had worked. And that came from a few things just clicking, right? These long-running agents that have these goals that they run at for long amounts of time, they have access to the right tools to do really effective work. What would that look like for non-engineers? What would that look like for the rest of the company? And so we landed on, we wanted to build a product where the work was organized around bots as the key operative principle, not around chats or around files or any other primitive. Second is that these bots should have access to the same tools that you do. I think it would be too much to expect these bots to actually contribute to a company without having their own computer, for example. We don't work every day with MCPs. So it's important that they can really use and operate the same tools a human does. And third is they should always be on. And I think we've seen this with loops and other engineering principles where if you can have these bots run for long amounts of time and be proactive and come to you with ideas or insights or things to take off of your plate, it's way more helpful than something that waits for you to poke and prod to actually do work. So that's what we built. We released it internally and I think one thing that was surprising from the initial reception was it was this bell curve internal feedback that we got where both people who were super AI forward, Lauren included, and people who were less AI forward, some of the least AI forward people in the company, both really enjoyed Grok Bot. It just clicked and it fit in their hands and their workflows in a particular way. And so then we brought it to market and I think we saw a lot of the same reception where it's easy to start with Grok Bot but the more you give it, the more you configure it to your life, the deeper you can get and the more powerful it can become. So the reception's been really exciting to see. There's still a lot more work to do and I think it's quite early. But that's a lot of how Grok Bot came to be.
turns.zh: 你们很多人都试过了，但对于那些还没试过的人，Grok Bot 旨在成为这样一个产品：你可以创建 AI 队友，我们是认真的。你可以给这些队友起名字、赋予身份、职能、技能和工具等等。我认为 Grok Bot 的由来是，它最初是我们短时间内快速搭建的内部原型。我们大约在七周内搭建了它。我们这么做部分是因为我们看到 AI 编程已经完全改变了我们工程师的工作方式。这源于几个因素的结合：这些长期运行的智能体有目标，会运行很长时间，它们能访问正确的工具来做真正有效的工作。那么对于非工程师来说，这会是什么样子？对于公司其他部门来说，这会是什么样子？所以我们决定，我们要构建一个产品，其中工作是以机器人为核心操作原则来组织的，而不是围绕聊天或文件或任何其他基本单元。其次，这些机器人应该能访问与你相同的工具。我认为，如果期望这些机器人没有自己的电脑就能真正为公司做贡献，那要求太高了。我们不是每天用 MCP 工作。所以重要的是它们能真正使用和操作与人类相同的工具。第三，它们应该始终在线。我想我们在循环和其他工程原则中已经看到了这一点：如果你能让这些机器人运行很长时间，主动向你提出想法或见解，或帮你分担任务，那它比那些等你戳一戳才干活的东西有用得多。这就是我们构建的东西。我们在内部发布了它，我认为最初反响中令人惊讶的一点是，我们得到了钟形曲线的内部反馈：无论是非常 AI 前沿的人，包括 Lauren，还是不太 AI 前沿的人，公司里一些最不 AI 前沿的人，都非常喜欢 Grok Bot。它就是很契合，以某种方式融入了他们的手头工作和流程。然后我们把它推向市场，我想我们看到了很多类似的反响：上手 Grok Bot 很容易，但你给它越多，你越把它配置到你的生活中，你就能越深入，它也能变得越强大。所以反响真的令人兴奋。还有很多工作要做，我认为这还很早。但这就是 Grok Bot 的由来。

turns.en: What are some of the use cases that you're seeing? Who's using Grok Bot and are there surprising ways that you've seen it being deployed in the wild?
turns.zh: 你们看到的一些用例是什么？谁在使用 Grok Bot？你们有没有看到它在实际应用中有令人惊讶的部署方式？

turns.en: I think we're starting to see it automate real functions inside of companies. And I think we've seen this pattern of people start using Grok Bot personally and maybe use it to do some basic task. They realize, wow, Grok Bot is pretty good at this thing. I'm going to trust my bot with more. I'm going to give it access to more tools. Instead of giving it a task, I might give it an outcome or an objective. Okay, it actually did a pretty good job with the objective. I'm going to just give it a full job now. Let's see how it can run with that. And I think especially outside of engineering, we're seeing this internally where, for example, our marketing team, our performance marketing team has just given their bot access to Google Ads and Facebook Ads, their own login. They give it a budget. They say, "Hey, I want you to talk to our design team's bot. They have a design bot that creates these assets and we're going to A/B test a bunch of them." So that's one example in marketing. Our support team. I think I started to see the way that a bot with access to the right tools can reproduce issues, can sit on top of the constant set of tickets that are coming in, maybe it can actually take some of these from beginning to end on its own. And so we're going to see more and more of this of domain experts inside of the company creating a bot, sharing it with the rest of the company and that bot being like an AI employee that is managed and has its own credentials and all the things you'd expect for a teammate. But how are you seeing it?
turns.zh: 我认为我们开始看到它自动化公司内部的真实职能。我们看到了这种模式：人们开始个人使用 Grok Bot，也许用它做一些基本任务。他们意识到，哇，Grok Bot 在这方面相当不错。我会更信任我的机器人。我会给它访问更多工具的权限。与其给它一个任务，我可能给它一个结果或目标。好吧，它实际上在目标上做得相当不错。我现在就给它一份完整的工作。看看它能怎么运行。我认为特别是在工程之外，我们在内部看到了这一点，例如，我们的营销团队、效果营销团队刚刚给了他们的机器人访问 Google Ads 和 Facebook Ads 的权限，用他们自己的登录。他们给它一个预算。他们说：“嘿，我想让你和我们设计团队的机器人沟通。他们有一个设计机器人来创建这些素材，我们要对一堆素材进行 A/B 测试。”所以这是营销中的一个例子。我们的支持团队。我开始看到，一个能访问正确工具的机器人可以重现问题，可以处理不断涌入的工单，也许它实际上可以自己从头到尾处理其中一些。所以我们将看到越来越多这样的情况：公司内部的领域专家创建一个机器人，与公司其他人分享，那个机器人就像一个 AI 员工，被管理着，有自己的凭证以及你对队友期望的所有东西。但你怎么看？

turns.en: For me, definitely I use Grok Bot a lot for my engineering work. I think where it made a big difference for me outside of the tools that we had before—like I use Cursor a lot—is the fact that Grok Bot forms my, I don't know if there's a good term for it, I like to call it my outer loop, where a lot of the work that I would do before in terms of gathering context for my bots or my agents—I would go to Slack, I would talk to my teammates, we would see an issue or a bug report or a feature request and then we'd talk about it and then I have to go off and summarize or copy-paste that into my bot. And the fact that Grok Bot has so many different connectors—you can add it to Slack now—just brings your agents with you to where the work is. And that makes it just so much more ergonomic for getting the context to the right place.
turns.zh: 对我来说，我肯定在工程工作中大量使用 Grok Bot。我认为它对我产生巨大影响的地方，除了我们之前有的工具——比如我经常用 Cursor——是 Grok Bot 形成了我的，我不知道有没有好的术语，我喜欢称之为我的外循环，以前我要做很多工作来为我的机器人或智能体收集上下文——我会去 Slack，和队友交流，我们会看到一个 issue 或 bug 报告或功能请求，然后讨论，然后我得去总结或复制粘贴到我的机器人里。而 Grok Bot 有这么多不同的连接器——你现在可以把它加到 Slack 里——它把你的智能体带到工作所在的地方。这使得把上下文放到正确的位置变得更加符合人体工学。

turns.en: So for me it's been really transformative in all the last mile, I call it the last mile, where before I was doing that by hand and now actually my bots are in that space with me and I can talk to them like a real co-worker in the Slack chat thread or even on X now, right? You can tag a bot and it feels so natural that it's really boosted my productivity.
turns.zh: 所以对我来说，它在整个最后一英里——我称之为最后一英里——真的很有变革性。以前我是手工做这些事，现在我的机器人就在那个空间里和我一起，我可以像真正的同事一样在 Slack 聊天线程里甚至现在在 X 上跟它们说话，对吧？你可以 @ 一个机器人，感觉非常自然，真的提升了我的生产力。

turns.en: Do you have personal bots that know, I mean they're in your email and then there's an email handling bot, or do you have one sort of work context bot that is watching all the channels and Slack and everything else?
turns.zh: 你有个人机器人吗？比如它们在收件箱里，有一个处理邮件的机器人，还是你有一个工作上下文机器人，监控所有频道、Slack 和其他一切？

turns.en: I think for me the beauty of Grok Bot is that you can create all these different bots. But how you split them up or how you set them up is very much up to you. What I like to tell people is you can set up your bots in a way that makes sense for your brain. So if you're the kind of person who likes to compartmentalize different pieces or buckets of work, then you can set up your bots that way. You can have specialist bots. I've also seen people do almost like a horizontal versus a vertical slice, where a horizontal slice might be I have one bot for every customer that I have, versus one bot for every function, every role, like an engineer bot, marketer bot. You could have one bot just for one customer that does everything, right? So I think it's really interesting to see how people have set up their bots. For me, I like to do it more horizontally. So I don't have a ton of bots, but I do have some specialists.
turns.zh: 对我来说，Grok Bot 的美妙之处在于你可以创建所有这些不同的机器人。但如何拆分它们或如何设置它们，很大程度上取决于你。我喜欢告诉人们的是，你可以按照适合你大脑的方式设置你的机器人。所以，如果你是那种喜欢把不同的工作分门别类的人，那么你可以那样设置你的机器人。你可以有专家机器人。我也见过人们做几乎像水平切片与垂直切片的划分，水平切片可能是我为每个客户有一个机器人，而垂直切片是为每个职能、每个角色，比如工程师机器人、营销人员机器人。你可以有一个机器人只为一个客户做所有事情，对吧？所以我觉得看到人们如何设置他们的机器人真的很有趣。对我来说，我更喜欢水平地做。所以我没有很多机器人，但我确实有一些专家机器人。

turns.en: That was like the first thing—I think one of my first DMs to you was like I love Grok Bot and then I was coming over from my OpenClaw world where I have like one bot named Wintermute and I'm like no no no I just want one bot and then now what I realize is each bot is actually its own context and then actually its own set of skills basically and loops are like sort of crons with web hooks on top of skill files right and then there's actually maps inside this world of having AI employees a lot better. Because you were saying earlier you guys had just talked to like all of you know some of your top users of Grok Bot and then surprisingly or maybe unsurprisingly some of the first ones that are most just like kind of crazy about it, they're actually small businesses which you wouldn't necessarily guess but on the other hand it was that they're the ones who struggle the most with hiring and so actually now out of pure necessity they're like hey this accounting thing that I can't hire someone to go do for me I can just go into Grok Bot and actually within the course of probably hours they have a new employee that does their bookkeeping probably perfectly actually.
turns.zh: 那就像第一件事——我想我给你的第一批私信之一就是我喜欢 Grok Bot，然后我从我的 OpenClaw 世界过来，那里我有一个叫 Wintermute 的机器人，我说不不不我只要一个机器人，然后现在我意识到每个机器人实际上是它自己的上下文，然后实际上是它自己的一套技能，而循环就像是基于技能文件的带有 web hook 的 cron 作业，对吧？然后在这个拥有 AI 员工的世界里实际上有地图，好多了。因为你之前说你们刚刚和所有你知道的一些 Grok Bot 的顶级用户聊过，然后令人惊讶或也许不令人惊讶的是，一些最早对它最疯狂的人，他们实际上是小企业，你不一定会猜到，但另一方面是因为他们是最难招聘的人，所以现在纯粹出于必要，他们说嘿，这个会计的事情我雇不到人来做，我可以直接去 Grok Bot，实际上大概在几个小时内他们就有了一个新员工，可能完美地做他们的簿记。

turns.en: Totally. Yeah, I think your point of some people just want one bot, some people want many bots—our goal is to build a product that fits in your hand no matter how you want to use it. I think there's a lot of flexibility to the tool and you can go deep when you need to. But one way that I organize my own bots, maybe similar to you, Lauren, is I kind of like having a bot that is solely dedicated to caring about a particular thing. And I think it maps onto my brain of the way that building a company, you like to think about hiring people: you like to hire someone who wakes up in the morning and really cares about a problem and they're thinking about it in the shower in the morning, they're on the way to work, they're just obsessive about a thing. And that maps in my mind much more clearly than one superstar superhuman person who simultaneously cares about a hundred things at once. And so in a lot of ways I have a small team of bots, but each of them care about a different thing and come to me proactively with what they're picking up on. And so I think to your point, as these bots really enter businesses and enter the workforce in a somewhat futuristic way, I think that's why small businesses and big businesses are seeing this bot identity thing really click for them: they say, 'Here's a business problem. I want a bot that cares about that business problem. I want it to be managed by the domain expert at the company who knows the most about that problem so that they can treat it like an apprentice.' And that feels very different than other AI solutions that have tried to solve similar problems that are a bit more omniscient or just kind of single approach to every problem.
turns.zh: 完全正确。是的，我认为你说的有些人只想要一个机器人，有些人想要很多机器人——我们的目标是构建一个适合你手头的产品，无论你想如何使用它。我认为这个工具非常灵活，你可以在需要时深入使用。但我组织自己机器人的一种方式，也许和你类似，Lauren，是我喜欢有一个专门关心某件事的机器人。我认为这符合我大脑中建立公司的方式，你喜欢考虑招聘人员：你喜欢雇一个早上醒来就真正关心一个问题的人，他们早上洗澡时都在想它，上班路上也在想，他们只是对一件事着迷。这在我脑海中比一个超级明星式的超人同时关心一百件事要清晰得多。所以很多时候我有一个小团队机器人，但每个都关心不同的事情，并主动向我汇报它们发现的东西。所以我认为正如你所说，当这些机器人真正进入企业并以某种未来主义的方式进入劳动力市场时，我认为这就是为什么小企业和大企业都看到这种机器人身份概念对他们来说真正奏效：他们说，‘这是一个业务问题。我想要一个关心那个业务问题的机器人。我希望它由公司中最了解那个问题的领域专家管理，这样他们可以把它当作学徒来对待。’这与尝试解决类似问题的其他 AI 解决方案感觉非常不同，那些方案有点更无所不知或对所有问题采用单一方法。

turns.en: And you support that now actually. Like you guys launched multiplayer for bots and there's sort of a bot master who has like right access and then you can share it across the org. Is that right?
turns.zh: 而你们现在实际上支持这个了。比如你们推出了机器人的多人模式，有一种机器人主控拥有权限，然后你可以在整个组织内共享它。对吗？

turns.en: Correct. Yeah. We—this was recent but about two weeks ago we launched team bots which are these bots that you can share with your team and I think the pattern we're seeing ourselves and we can give a few examples is there's a person at a company who is a bit more of a builder, they enjoy building these tools. I think inside of the engineering department there are many people like this but I think we're finding that in other departments, you know, GTM engineers or support engineers, people like that really love taking a few hours of their day to build these scalable automations that can take work off of the plates of their peers and kind of the company.
turns.zh: 正确。是的。我们——这是最近的事，大约两周前我们推出了团队机器人，这些机器人你可以与团队共享。我认为我们自己看到的模式——我们可以举几个例子——是公司里有一个人更像构建者，他们喜欢构建这些工具。我认为在工程部门里有很多这样的人，但我觉得我们在其他部门也发现，你知道，GTM 工程师或支持工程师，这样的人真的喜欢花几个小时构建这些可扩展的自动化，从而减轻同事和公司的工作负担。

turns.en: I guess one thing that brings to mind is basically went through maybe it was a year ago-ish when Steve posted the whole gas city post that then started software factories—gas sorry it was gas town—that started software factories where a lot of engineers have been using this inner loop and I think you've been building now this outer loop that you were mentioning Lauren, right? turns.zh: 我认为我们在负责 Grok Bot 的核心团队中看到了这一点。Lauren 每月提交 4,000 个 PR。我认为我们会开始看到更多工程师这样做。我们开始看到瓶颈不再是投入开发这些想法和功能的时间或工程资源。实际上，更多的是我们团队之间的对齐，比如我们希望产品路线图是什么？我们的愿景是什么？什么是好的？什么是伟大的？我认为我们正在看到这一点，Lauren 和我进行了很多讨论，我们谈论 Grok Bot 的未来变化，有人提出一个建议，然后房间里的另一个人说：‘哦，如果你感兴趣，我有一个 PR。我周末一直在做这个。’这种情况经常发生。所以东西已经建好了，但我们不想全部合并，因为那会导致一个有点弗兰肯斯坦式的产品，夹杂着随机的副项目。我们确实需要一致的产品愿景和哲学。所以我认为我们现在把更多时间转移到这些问题上，因为每个人每天或每周都在做成千上万的微观决策，我认为过去不是这样。

transcript.sec: Taste and discernment in product decisions

turns.en: Which actually I'm very curious. I mean this is a bit of the trendy thing now with the thing that matters is taste which means actually saying no to a bunch of stuff and having discernment. What does that look like in practice for you guys? How do you make a decision yes or no on this?
turns.zh: 其实我非常好奇。我的意思是，现在有点流行说重要的是品味，这意味着实际上要对一堆东西说不，要有辨别力。对你们来说，这在实践中是什么样子的？你们如何决定是或否？

turns.en: Yeah. For certain category of things. So Lauren has set up one of my favorite parts of our factory is Sandy, which takes in thousands of pieces of customer feedback every day. We receive it through the product. We receive it through our support channels. We receive it through X. And a lot of times there are just small bugs. And so in a lot of cases, Lauren's factory just fixes it like refros, fixes, merges. No one thinks about it.
turns.zh: 是的。对于某些类别的事情。Lauren 设置了我们工厂中我最喜欢的部分之一，Sandy，它每天接收数千条客户反馈。我们通过产品接收，通过支持渠道接收，通过 X 接收。很多时候只是小 bug。所以在很多情况下，Lauren 的工厂只是修复它，比如重构、修复、合并。没人会多想。

turns.en: It goes out automatically at 3 in the morning.
turns.zh: 它在凌晨 3 点自动发布。

turns.en: I wish all software would be made that way. I wish Apple people who work at Apple could do this because hey I have you know calendar team in particular I have some problems with you.
turns.zh: 我希望所有软件都能那样制作。我希望在 Apple 工作的人能做到这一点，因为嘿，尤其是日历团队，我对你们有些意见。

turns.en: There's a lot of Grok Bot that should be self-healing in that way and it's cool that that finally works. I think there's another set of questions that should not operate that way at all. If you're changing the core pixels that a user is experiencing every day, it's really frustrating as a user to wake up and you refresh your Grok Bot and there's a whole new—the button moved and then it moved again the next day. And so the way we try to counteract that is a lot of dogfooding internally. And sitting with a change for longer than feels comfortable before we ship it. And the default is if something doesn't get internal product market fit, we don't ship it. Even if it gets like mixed internal product market fit, we don't ship it. And so as a team, we really try to keep a high bar.
turns.zh: Grok Bot 有很多部分应该以那种方式自我修复，很高兴这终于奏效了。我认为还有另一类问题完全不应该那样运作。如果你在改变用户每天体验的核心像素，作为用户，醒来刷新你的 Grok Bot，发现按钮移动了，然后第二天又移动了，这真的很令人沮丧。所以我们试图抵消这种情况的方法是大量内部吃自己的狗粮。在发布之前，让变更停留的时间比感觉舒适的时间更长。默认情况下，如果某个东西没有获得内部产品市场契合，我们就不发布。即使获得混合的内部产品市场契合，我们也不发布。所以作为一个团队，我们真的努力保持高标准。

turns.en: Yeah, I think that's actually one of my favorite parts of working on the Grok Bot team is that, despite the great velocity that we have, we still have a lot of intention and care for the user experience. And even though you can go really fast, it doesn't mean that you should just ship every feature you can think of. And this is where human judgment and taste, I think, comes in. I don't think that's going to go out of style, personally. I think as long as we're building software for humans, humans should really be thinking about the intentionally designed experience because we know each other the best, right? If you're building software for agents, that's a different story that you can certainly probably go as fast as possible, but I think, yeah, for humans, you do want to have put intentional care and thought into the stuff that you develop. So even for my own factories, I don't turn them towards feature development. I turn them more towards the software maintenance side of things because I care a lot about performance. I care a lot about fixing bugs that our users encounter or quality of life complaints that they have. And I think that's actually such a great use of the agents because that used to be like a full-time job for someone and now I've given that to a lot of agents and that frees me up and other engineers up to think more intensely about the product experience.
turns.zh: 是的，我认为这实际上是我在 Grok Bot 团队工作中最喜欢的部分之一，尽管我们速度很快，但我们仍然对用户体验有很多意图和关怀。即使你可以非常快，也不意味着你应该发布你能想到的每一个功能。我认为这就是人类判断力和品味发挥作用的地方。我个人不认为这会过时。我认为只要我们在为人类构建软件，人类就应该真正思考精心设计的体验，因为我们最了解彼此，对吧？如果你在为智能体构建软件，那是另一回事，你当然可以尽可能快，但我认为，对于人类，你确实需要对你开发的东西投入有意的关怀和思考。所以即使对我自己的工厂，我也不把它们转向功能开发。我更多地把它们转向软件维护方面，因为我非常关心性能。我非常关心修复用户遇到的 bug 或他们提出的生活质量投诉。我认为这实际上是智能体的一个很好的用途，因为那曾经是某人的全职工作，现在我把这个交给很多智能体，这释放了我和其他工程师，让我们更集中地思考产品体验。

transcript.sec: Lauren's journey from finance to AI engineering

turns.en: One thing that's very inspiring about your journey, Lauren, I don't know if many people know is you grew up in Singapore and you studied a non-technical degree. You did a bachelor's in accounting and finance from in Australia. Then somehow you ended up becoming one of the now best AI engineers.
turns.zh: Lauren，你的旅程中有一件非常鼓舞人心的事，我不知道有多少人知道，你在新加坡长大，你学的是非技术学位。你在澳大利亚获得了会计和金融学士学位。然后不知怎么的，你成为了现在最好的 AI 工程师之一。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: How did that happen? I think sometimes people think it's very hard to get into tech, but you did it. And you also worked on the React compiler which is one of the hardest things as well.
turns.zh: 那是怎么发生的？我认为有时人们认为进入科技行业很难，但你做到了。你还参与了 React 编译器的工作，这也是最难的事情之一。

turns.en: Yeah. I think I've definitely feel like I've had a very privileged and lucky experience in the tech. I think that was a time where people were much more open to the idea of a self-taught developer. So I guess the long story short is after college I did study finance. One of my favorite courses was actually financial modeling and we learned how to use Excel and Visual Basic for Applications to make some cool financial valuations and things like that. And through the course of that course, I realized I had more fun building the spreadsheet and the macros than I did the finance part. I mean, the finance part was interesting, too. But the technical part, thinking logically, just was really interesting to me and something I hadn't really thought I was cut out for. So, after college, I started a startup with a friend, a classmate.
turns.zh: 是的。我确实觉得自己在科技行业有一段非常幸运的经历。我认为那是一个人们对自学开发者的想法更加开放的时代。所以长话短说，大学毕业后我确实学了金融。我最喜欢的课程之一实际上是财务建模，我们学习了如何使用 Excel 和 Visual Basic for Applications 来制作一些很酷的财务估值等等。通过那门课程，我意识到我构建电子表格和宏比做金融部分更有趣。我的意思是，金融部分也很有趣。但技术部分，逻辑思考，对我来说真的很有趣，而且是我以前认为自己不适合的事情。所以，大学毕业后，我和一个朋友、一个同学一起创办了一家初创公司。

turns.en: It didn't go super far, but we learned a lot from that process, and I got really involved with the startup community in Australia. That's how I got my first job. And really, the secret that I attribute for my success is actually X.
turns.zh: 它没有走得很远，但我们从那个过程中学到了很多，我也真正融入了澳大利亚的创业社区。我就是这样得到了第一份工作。而真正让我成功的秘诀其实是 X。

turns.en: I started out when I was still basically learning how to code. I had a blog and I was just sharing what I learned. And I was fortunate enough that someone from the framework community—the JavaScript framework Ember that I was building my application in—
turns.zh: 我开始的时候基本上还在学怎么编程。我有一个博客，只是分享我学到的东西。我很幸运，框架社区里有人——我当时用 JavaScript 框架 Ember 构建应用——

turns.en: So yeah, Tom Dale and Leah Silber, they reached out to me and said, 'Would you be interested in giving a talk at the conference that's coming up in Portland, Oregon?' And I was very shocked because I had never even been to a conference in my life. And then now I was being asked to talk at a conference with like hundreds of people. And you know, public speaking was always my worst fear. But somehow they convinced me to do it.
turns.zh: 所以是的，Tom Dale 和 Leah Silber 联系了我，说：‘你有兴趣在即将于俄勒冈州波特兰举行的会议上做个演讲吗？’我非常震惊，因为我这辈子从未参加过会议。而现在我被邀请在一个有几百人的会议上演讲。你知道，公开演讲一直是我最大的恐惧。但不知怎么的，他们说服了我去做。

turns.en: I learned about the ability of being able to communicate your ideas and bring people along in that journey. And this skill of storytelling and communication has really stuck with me, even though I've been really involved with engineering work. And I've had a lot of really great mentors as well in the past.
turns.zh: 我学到了能够传达你的想法并带领人们一起踏上这段旅程的能力。而这种讲故事和沟通的技能真的一直伴随着我，尽管我一直深入参与工程工作。而且我过去也有很多非常棒的导师。

turns.en: So I think all that to say is: do cool stuff, talk about the cool stuff, and just keep doing that in the loop. And maybe the stars will align and someone will notice something you said on X and retweet you, offer you an opportunity that you hadn't had before. Maybe you develop your idea and you come up with a startup idea, right? And then you go apply to YC, and before you know it, you could change your life with just a tweet.
turns.zh: 所以我想总而言之就是：做酷的事情，谈论酷的事情，然后在这个循环中不断做下去。也许星星会对齐，有人会注意到你在 X 上说的话并转发，给你一个你从未有过的机会。也许你发展你的想法，想出了一个创业点子，对吧？然后你去申请 YC，不知不觉中，你就能仅仅通过一条推文改变你的生活。

turns.en: It's a great place to end. I think Lauren Roman, thank you guys so much for joining us.
turns.zh: 这是一个很好的结束点。我想 Lauren Roman，非常感谢你们加入我们。

turns.en: It was so fun.
turns.zh: 太有趣了。

turns.en: Thank you for making an incredible product. So, can't wait to see what you build from here.
turns.zh: 感谢你们做出了一个不可思议的产品。所以，迫不及待想看看你们从这里开始会构建什么。

turns.en: Thanks for having us. It was a lot of fun.
turns.zh: 感谢邀请我们。非常有趣。

tldr.en: Grok Bot treats AI as teammates with identities, tools, and proactive presence, not just chats.
tldr.zh: Grok Bot 将 AI 视为拥有身份、工具和主动性的队友，而非单纯的聊天工具。

tldr.en: Trust in bots grows in stages: read-only, then action-taking, then owning a job.
tldr.zh: 对机器人的信任分阶段建立：先只读，再执行操作，最后负责整个任务。

tldr.en: As execution becomes abundant, the bottleneck shifts to intent specification, vision, and taste.
tldr.zh: 随着执行能力变得充裕，瓶颈转向意图明确、愿景和品味。
